drafts.subject: chr:entity:augustus
drafts.quotation: he was carried in a small boat to his right wing
drafts.rationale: The passage opens with 'he', who is Caesar. The surrounding sections (65.2, 65.3, 65.5) show this is Caesar, who posted Agrippa on the left and kept the right wing for himself. Per the inquiry guidance, Caesar means Octavian/Augustus. He is on the right wing facing the enemy fleet as Antony's left wing begins to move.
drafts.relevance: It places Octavian (Augustus) in person with his fleet at the Battle of Actium as the engagement opens.
ambiguities: The subject is only the pronoun 'he'; the identification as Caesar/Octavian comes from the surrounding sections.
The action described is largely pre-engagement positioning, and the passage ends just as Antony's left wing begins to move, so whether this counts as presence in the engagement is uncertain.
